subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support LLM-driven contextual activation for unmentioned group traffic, and what consent, provider-exposure, config, logging, retention, and core-versus-plugin ownership contract should govern it?
rationale: Automation can prove the feature is missing, but cannot choose the privacy boundary, public config shape, provider exposure, logging retention, or long-term owner for processing unmentioned group messages.

options.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design for consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and validation before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Narrow to ambient or attention modes
options.body: Pursue timer-based attention windows or documented ambient room-event ergonomics without adding background LLM peeking yet.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API seam
options.body: Design the observation and decision-hook API needed to keep this optional policy outside core runtime defaults.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design for consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and validation before accepting implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across the group activation command, inbound mention policy, and cross-channel gating surfaces that define this boundary.
